subject: System Design
title: Conflict Resolution Strategies
description: A micro-lesson that makes Conflict Resolution Strategies usable.

hook.text: Two users edit the same document on different continents. Both changes arrive at the server. Which wins?

buildup.text: Last Write Wins (LWW) picks the most recent write by timestamp. Simple, but it silently drops the other.

discovery.text: Application-level resolution lets the app merge both changes — like Git's merge for user data.

twist.text: LWW with clock skew can discard the truly latest write. Timestamps across machines are never perfectly synced.

climax.text: There's no universal conflict resolution. The right strategy depends on your data model and user expectations.

punchline.text: Conflicts are inevitable — the resolution strategy defines correctness.

quiz.question: What is the problem with Last Write Wins?
options: Clock skew can cause the wrong write to be kept
